transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

I came in because I keep getting stuck doing things at the register that don’t fit the moment. Like tapping the scanner in a pattern, or just freezing with my hand over the cash drawer while a customer is waiting. Last week I got written up for it.
When you freeze like that, are you fully aware of what is happening around you?
Yeah, I’m aware of the customer and everything around me. I just sort of get stuck—my hand will be over the drawer, or I’ll be tapping the scanner, and I can’t seem to stop and move on right away.
When you find yourself tapping or freezing like that, is there a specific thought, worry, or rule in your mind that makes you feel you have to do it?

No, not really. There isn’t a thought or rule behind it that I can point to. I just find myself tapping the scanner or sitting there with my hand over the drawer, even though the customer is waiting and I know I should keep going.
Have you ever noticed yourself making repetitive sounds or noises, such as throat clearing, grunting, or vocal outbursts, that you feel unable to stop?
No, I haven’t really noticed making sounds like that.
Right before you tap or freeze, do you feel an uncomfortable physical sensation or urge building up inside that goes away after you do it?
No, I don’t feel an urge building up or anything like that. It just happens—I’ll start tapping the scanner in a pattern, or freeze with my hand over the drawer, even though the customer’s waiting.
Around what age did you first start noticing these repetitive movements?
I’m not sure when it first started. It’s become a problem at the register lately, though—like tapping the scanner or just freezing with my hand over the cash drawer.
Have any of these repetitive movements or actions ever caused you physical pain or injury?
No, I haven’t hurt myself from it. It’s mostly caused problems at work—last week I got written up because I froze at the register while a customer was waiting.
